approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent prior from the supplied unlabeled SMILES, always conditioning each next-token prediction on the intact preceding tokens. Its fixed holdout chooses the prior checkpoint. Each objective then starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The best current observations train together with a uniform sample from a memory of the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted rewards. Bounded prior-likelihood-plus-reward updates adapt the policy, which samples complete new molecules with chemical and duplicate checks. The prior has not been trained to recover after a small amount of context information is missing.
approach.novelty: During each unlabeled training sequence, hide exactly one randomly selected content-token embedding and still predict the original unmodified targets with the existing equal-token loss. The rest of the sequence remains visible. This asks the recurrent state to use surrounding context instead of depending entirely on one local input. Clean strings and the original clean holdout still determine checkpoint selection, and online learning and generation use ordinary intact inputs. Earlier siblings changed bracket units, equivalent string views or branch loss allocation; this Child tests robustness to one missing internal context vector without changing those mechanisms. A successful robustness result still has to translate into useful valid new molecules.

hypothesis: Train the unlabeled recurrent prior to predict the unchanged original SMILES targets after zeroing exactly one uniformly selected eligible content-token input embedding per sequence, while keeping the Parent uniform token loss, clean fixed-holdout checkpoint selection and all online computations unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Missing-context prediction improved sharply, but validity and final molecular scores declined
finding_summary.insights: The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.
finding_summary.results: The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. Mean zaleplon score rose by 0.03533, while sitagliptin fell by 0.08046 and lost score in every seed. The intended +0.002 macro improvement was not achieved.

molecular.headline: Mostly conventional aromatic amides, amines and sulfonamides, with extreme polar or lipophilic tails and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is broadly diverse and mainly resembles ordinary medicinal chemistry: aryl amides and ureas, heteroaromatic amino compounds, indanol/tetralin-like alcohols, piperazines, sulfonamides, cyclic carbonyl compounds and ether-linked heterocycles. Most leading structures have plausible synthetic entry points and conventional bonding. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9793 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.946 to 0.992. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.4 to 50.5, while the low tails include much larger peptides, polyamines, sugars, macrocycles and long hydrocarbon chains. Charged-token rates range from 0.0368 to 0.1299 and include ordinary nitro, azide and ammonium representations as well as occasional unusual electronic states; these rates are not a measure of solution ionization. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the parent strings, leaving substituted saturated-ring alcohols and other stereogenic products undefined. The chemistry is generally plausible and moderately drug-like, but chemical plausibility alone does not explain the score variation, and individual reactive or geometrically difficult alternatives remain.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are moderate-sized aromatic amides or diaryl ureas, with methoxy phenyl or pyridyl groups, another aryl ring and a pyridyl or pyrimidyl carbonyl partner. Connections vary between methylene, direct biaryl and diarylamino arrangements. The molecules have recognizable amide/urea donors and acceptors, mostly ordinary aromatic substitution and little stereochemical complexity. They are generally synthetically plausible. The lowest examples are substantially larger peptide-like structures, highly hydroxylated or phosphorylated compounds, a long-ring polyamine and a very small cyanide species. Final molecules range from appropriate aromatic amides to much simpler hydrocarbons or heteroarenes that lose the polar-linker arrangement.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic rings with flexible methylene or amino links can increase conformational freedom even when the individual bonds are ordinary.
Peptide-like and highly hydroxylated proposals introduce substantial size or polarity outside the leading families.
Small charged fragments and isolated unusual electronic-state variants occur in the wider trajectories despite the conventional leading chemistry.
missing_features: Low peptide-like, polyol and macrocyclic products lack the compact aromatic and carbonyl-linker organization of the leading molecules.
The simpler low final heteroarenes lack the amide/urea arrangement retained by the stronger examples; aromatic content alone is insufficient.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule. That is a coverage difference rather than proof that an indole is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Several different methoxy diarylmethyl heteroaryl amides and a methoxypyridyl/diaryl urea all score 0.48839749189747395. Related diarylamino and alternative pyridyl amides score 0.4767312946227961. These ties support a relatively compact aromatic/polar-linker balance without identifying one uniquely required ring nitrogen position or linkage. An aromatic tertiary amide in the final set scores 0.4155143263564241, whereas a naphthalene-pyridine without the amide arrangement scores 0.0019315588620192265. The large peptide-like low example scores 1.2479689558218067e-56. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a substituted indole carboxamide, while current seed 0 reaches 0.48839749189747395 with diarylmethyl amides. Current seed 1 and seed 2 reach 0.48839749189747395 and 0.4540824430539665 versus parental 0.4067656765249372 and 0.3900700429110833. The new leading chemistry is conventional, but the comparisons do not isolate a single missing pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are aromatic nitrogen heterocycles bearing arylamino groups, alkoxy substitution, nitrile or trifluoromethyl groups and, in the leader, a nitroanilide carboxamide. Other strong families include amino-linked fused diones, ordinary aryl sulfonamides and acylhydrazones. These are generally moderate to bulky, planar or partly planar medicinal-chemistry structures with recognizable synthetic connections. The low examples include a large ester/amide/methylsulfone assembly, an indole ether-acetamide/benzothiazole combination and a sulfone-substituted indole. Small acyclic or fluorocarbon fragments sit close to the low baseline. The output has abundant aromatic and heteroatom content but its placement matters.
liabilities: Several leading compounds carry extensive aromatic and fluorinated substitution with little saturated shape diversity.
Nitroaryl, acylhydrazone and thioether variants have distinct chemical liabilities that are not resolved by their similar scores.
A low charged nitrogen/oxygen fragment has an unusual electronic-state representation, so charge tokens should not be interpreted as uniformly ordinary ionization chemistry.
missing_features: The small low-baseline fragments lack the connected aromatic and polar-linker organization of the stronger products.

The low but synthetically plausible multiaryl structures show that merely including heterocycles, an amide or oxidized sulfur does not preserve the useful arrangement. Matched attachment-position and ring-nitrogen variants remain incompletely explored in the displayed leaders.
Less aromatic, more saturated shape variants retaining the useful polar fragments are limited among the strongest examples; their potential score benefit is not established by this set.

Replacing that carboxanilide appendage by methoxy in the same broader scaffold family gives 0.6076219961668878; a nitrile relative scores 0.6056754360035471. Amino-linked diones with ethylthio, methoxy or propargyloxy substitution all score 0.6014089846464902, so those peripheral groups are not uniquely distinguished. An aryl sulfonamide reaches 0.5999223218699244, whereas a differently arranged sulfone-indole scores 0.31752369822101023 and an indole/benzothiazole amide scores 0.3004981574996588. This is evidence for particular heteroaromatic/linker arrangements, not a general sulfur penalty or reward. Current per-seed maxima are 0.6111751890298603, 0.5908091850309445 and 0.5784746092483299, compared with parental 0.5913471190523991, 0.61192894944948 and 0.5758665324320438. per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are conventional aryl- or pyridyl-piperazines connected through ether/alkyl or aminoalkyl chains to indanol- or tetralin-like frameworks. Alcohol, methoxy, amino and aryl halogen substituents vary around the fused ring. The products combine available aliphatic amines with aromatic surface and a polar alcohol or ether. Seed 2 also produces flexible biaryl compounds with an expanded diaza ring and a nitrile-bearing phenoxyethyl connection. These are recognizable synthetic families. Low examples are amide, ester, sulfonamide or hydrazone-dominated compounds lacking the same organized aliphatic-amine framework, although one low structure does contain a primary amine.
liabilities: Flexible alkyl chains and several potentially basic centres introduce conformational and ionization ambiguity.
Unspecified alcohol and substituted-ring stereochemistry prevents the leading structures from describing single defined stereoisomers.
Other seeds include an organic azide among stronger products, so the conventional main piperazine family does not imply uniform stability across the full output.
missing_features: The low amide/sulfonamide series lacks the accessible aliphatic amine placement and hydrophobic-ring spacing of the stronger piperazine families.
The low primary-amine-containing urea shows that a basic centre without the useful overall arrangement is insufficient; matched linker geometry and ring-size comparisons are still needed.
The leading alcohol-bearing fused rings have potential stereogenic centres but no specified configurations. No stereochemical preference can be read from the supplied unlabelled molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoroindanol/propoxy/pyridylpiperazine molecule scores 0.999998460810131; its nonfluorinated indanol relative scores 0.9999948760798478. Several aminoalkyl/tetralin-like alternatives also approach 1.0, and matched aryl fluorine/chlorine substitutions have identical recorded values of 0.9999949345268564 or 0.9999929302907594. These nearly equal values support the general aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement but do not establish a unique halogen or fused-ring size requirement. The lowest amide-rich example scores 3.243749221679736e-05, while a primary-amine-containing but differently connected urea scores 6.812931663695377e-05; amine presence alone is not enough. Parent seed 1 already had an indole/alkyl/arylpiperazine leader at 0.9999999999666845. per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules include an N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide attached to a fused benzoxazolinone-like cyclic carbamate, and a benzodioxole-sulfonyl piperazine bearing a benzodioxole acetamide side chain. Other stronger examples are a benzodioxole-substituted fused aromatic lactam, imidazole-like compounds, aromatic amides and sulfonamides. These have conventional amine, carbonyl, ether and oxidized sulfur functionality and are mostly synthetically plausible. Low products include flexible acyclic polyamines, small sulfur-containing acids, a saturated cage amide and a small carbonyl-containing oxygen/sulfur ring. The final molecules span complex sulfonamide assemblies and simpler structures lacking the same aromatic/polar arrangement.
liabilities: Large sulfonamide/amide combinations can add aromatic bulk and polarity while scoring below a simpler leader.
Some saturated or fused alternatives have undefined stereochemical relationships, although the principal piperazine leaders are achiral.
Small fragments and highly flexible charged or polyamine products can lose the aromatic organization retained by the stronger structures.
missing_features: The low flexible polyamines and small sulfur-containing acids lack the integrated aromatic/carbonyl or sulfonyl/amine arrangement found in the stronger molecules.
The displayed leaders incompletely sample matched aromatic partners and linker placements around the sulfonyl-piperazine arrangement; larger or more polar appendages are not automatically beneficial.

The trajectories do not identify one uniquely missing group beyond these observed associations. The remaining chemistry gap concerns compatible connectivity and shape rather than adding piperazine or sulfur indiscriminately.

A flexible acyclic polyamine/polyether scores 0.0, a small sulfur-ring acid scores 0.026148818018424533, and a more complex saturated cage amide scores 0.04076048393103888. The final methoxyaryl piperazine amide reaches only 0.1411862416005035, showing that piperazine alone is not sufficient. per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a diarylethyl-substituted aminoguanidine hydrazone, combining aromatic hydrophobic groups with a strongly polar imino/nitrogen-rich head. Other stronger products are quite different: a pyrrolidine linked to a small sulfonylated diaza ring with an oxime-like group, an ester/amide-substituted aromatic pyridone, an oxalamide with a bridged saturated amine, and ether-linked triazole/imidazole-like heterocycles. Most fragments are familiar, but hydrazone configuration, small-ring strain and ionization remain unresolved. The lowest products are very long lipids or polyamines, highly hydroxylated sugar/nucleoside-like compounds and other bulky flexible molecules. There is no dominant shared high-scoring ring family.
liabilities: The aminoguanidine hydrazone combines a potentially strongly basic head with an unassigned imine configuration and an N-N connection.
The sulfonylated diaza/oxime alternative contains a strained small nitrogen ring, while other candidates introduce bridged saturated rings without stereochemical definition.
Extreme hydrocarbon chains, long polyamine chains and sugar-rich structures dominate some low-score examples, despite being chemically very different from each other.
missing_features: The lowest long-chain, polymer-like and highly hydroxylated products lack the moderate scale and localized polar/aromatic organization of the better examples.

The supplied leaders are too chemically disparate to establish a single unseen functional group as the answer. Matched series preserving a useful polar-linker arrangement while varying size, geometry and ionization-relevant groups are missing from the displayed evidence.
The stronger parental carbonyl and polar-ring arrangements are not represented among the current leaders as closely matched alternatives.
Hydrazone or oxime geometry and possible saturated-ring stereochemistry are not specified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminoguanidine hydrazone scores 0.2320107079772056; the sulfonylated small diaza-ring/oxime compound scores 0.23124825514969893, and the aromatic ester/amide/pyridone scores 0.22293874669174316. A methoxyaryl/heterocycle ether reaches 0.1871471057147747, while a related ethoxyaryl ketone reaches 0.15125101854430076; additional peripheral changes mean this is not a single-bond comparison. These observations support moderate size and particular localized polar/aromatic arrangements, but do not identify a universal carbonyl, basic amine, fluorine or heterocycle requirement. Long-chain lipid and polyamine examples score 0.0, and a sugar-rich structure scores 9.167234704499243e-127. The digest reports a median of 0.0. Current per-seed maxima are 0.2320107079772056, 0.23124825514969893 and 0.1871471057147747, versus parental 0.2932061327730367, 0.28770317918999355 and 0.3108657757276207. The current chemistry is plausible in many cases but does not recover the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low examples include long lipids, long polyamine chains, highly hydroxylated sugars, peptide-like molecules and small polar fragments. Better molecules instead combine moderate aromatic frameworks with localized amide, urea, sulfonyl, amine or ether functionality. Both very hydrophobic and very polar extremes can have recorded scores of 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular scale or balance of aromatic and polar functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemical variations that preserve a promising size and functional-group arrangement while changing scaffold or linker geometry. Avoid making local variation depend on large chain growth, excessive polar repetition or deletion of most of the useful framework.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A low primary-amine-containing urea scores 6.812931663695377e-05 despite the success of several piperazine/aryl-amine families. An ordinary aryl sulfonamide reaches 0.5999223218699244 while a differently arranged sulfone-indole scores 0.31752369822101023. A final piperazine amide scores 0.1411862416005035 versus 0.2189839359276689 for a compact sulfonyl-piperazine/aromatic-carbonyl combination.
transferable_gaps.gap: Matched spatial arrangements are incompletely represented even when the useful functional groups are already available.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate coherent matched series varying attachment position, linker length, ring nitrogen placement and saturation while retaining the rest of the framework. Do not substitute simple counts of amines, rings or sulfur groups for the chemical arrangement supported by feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The strongest alcohol-bearing indanol/tetralin-like products have possible stereogenic centres, and other displayed molecules contain substituted pyrrolidines, bridged rings, hydrazones or oxime-like groups. Many aromatic amide and piperazine leaders are achiral, so the missing definition is structure-dependent.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic alcohol and saturated-ring products, and configurationally variable imines, remain undefined.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Specify feasible absolute and relative configurations, and imine or oxime geometry where relevant, and preserve them during structural changes. Compare matched configurations without treating stereochemical labels as universally necessary or automatically beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several different aromatic amide and urea arrangements share 0.48839749189747395. Ethylthio, methoxy and propargyloxy relatives share 0.6014089846464902, while multiple aryl fluorine/chlorine pairs have identical near-maximum scores. These observations do not demonstrate a unique need for the more elaborate appendages.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simple alternatives are not consistently distinguished from extra functionality whose local score contribution is unclear.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that reduce flexible chains, excess substitution or reactive functionality while retaining the useful core arrangement. Use observed feedback to determine which simpler structures preserve the desired chemistry.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

finding_summary.headline: Missing-context prediction improved sharply, but validity and final molecular scores declined
finding_summary.insights: The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.
finding_summary.results: The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. Mean zaleplon score rose by 0.03533, while sitagliptin fell by 0.08046 and lost score in every seed. The intended +0.002 macro improvement was not achieved.

finding_summary.headline: Missing-context prediction improved sharply, but validity and final molecular scores declined
finding_summary.insights: The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.

molecular_assessment.headline: Mostly conventional aromatic amides, amines and sulfonamides, with extreme polar or lipophilic tails and undefined stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is broadly diverse and mainly resembles ordinary medicinal chemistry: aryl amides and ureas, heteroaromatic amino compounds, indanol/tetralin-like alcohols, piperazines, sulfonamides, cyclic carbonyl compounds and ether-linked heterocycles. Most leading structures have plausible synthetic entry points and conventional bonding. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9793 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.946 to 0.992. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.4 to 50.5, while the low tails include much larger peptides, polyamines, sugars, macrocycles and long hydrocarbon chains. Charged-token rates range from 0.0368 to 0.1299 and include ordinary nitro, azide and ammonium representations as well as occasional unusual electronic states; these rates are not a measure of solution ionization. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the parent strings, leaving substituted saturated-ring alcohols and other stereogenic products undefined. The chemistry is generally plausible and moderately drug-like, but chemical plausibility alone does not explain the score variation, and individual reactive or geometrically difficult alternatives remain.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are moderate-sized aromatic amides or diaryl ureas, with methoxy phenyl or pyridyl groups, another aryl ring and a pyridyl or pyrimidyl carbonyl partner. Connections vary between methylene, direct biaryl and diarylamino arrangements. The molecules have recognizable amide/urea donors and acceptors, mostly ordinary aromatic substitution and little stereochemical complexity. They are generally synthetically plausible. The lowest examples are substantially larger peptide-like structures, highly hydroxylated or phosphorylated compounds, a long-ring polyamine and a very small cyanide species. Final molecules range from appropriate aromatic amides to much simpler hydrocarbons or heteroarenes that lose the polar-linker arrangement.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic rings with flexible methylene or amino links can increase conformational freedom even when the individual bonds are ordinary.
Peptide-like and highly hydroxylated proposals introduce substantial size or polarity outside the leading families.
Small charged fragments and isolated unusual electronic-state variants occur in the wider trajectories despite the conventional leading chemistry.
missing_features: Low peptide-like, polyol and macrocyclic products lack the compact aromatic and carbonyl-linker organization of the leading molecules.
The simpler low final heteroarenes lack the amide/urea arrangement retained by the stronger examples; aromatic content alone is insufficient.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule. That is a coverage difference rather than proof that an indole is universally required.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent prior from the supplied unlabeled SMILES, always conditioning each next-token prediction on the intact preceding tokens. Its fixed holdout chooses the prior checkpoint. Each objective then starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The best current observations train together with a uniform sample from a memory of the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted rewards. Bounded prior-likelihood-plus-reward updates adapt the policy, which samples complete new molecules with chemical and duplicate checks. The prior has not been trained to recover after a small amount of context information is missing.
approach.novelty: During each unlabeled training sequence, hide exactly one randomly selected content-token embedding and still predict the original unmodified targets with the existing equal-token loss. The rest of the sequence remains visible. This asks the recurrent state to use surrounding context instead of depending entirely on one local input. Clean strings and the original clean holdout still determine checkpoint selection, and online learning and generation use ordinary intact inputs. Earlier siblings changed bracket units, equivalent string views or branch loss allocation; this Child tests robustness to one missing internal context vector without changing those mechanisms. A successful robustness result still has to translate into useful valid new molecules.
